when: Sentence 1 of every Task 1 report: replace 'shows' from the question (structure: The chart/graph + shows/illustrates + what + where + when)

items.pattern: The [chart type] illustrates + what + where + when
items.example: The line graph illustrates the proportion of Australian exports to four distinct countries over the period from 1990 to 2012.
items.note: Teacher's first choice. Never copy the question word for word.

items.example: The line graph presents data on the percentage of people residing in Australia who came from different parts of the world over the period from 1976 to 2011.

items.phrase: gives information on / gives data on
items.example: The bar chart gives information on the number of seals, whales and dolphins recorded in the Gormez Straits between 2006 and 2018.
items.note: Teacher's handout: shows -> illustrates / gives information on / depicts / describes.

items.example: The table depicts the percentage of women in senior management positions in three companies between 1975 and 2015.
The pie chart indicates four primary causes of farmland becoming degraded in the world.
The bar chart compares the annual pay of doctors and other workers in seven countries in 2004.
items.note: Good when the visual sets two or more groups side by side.

items.pattern: The chart illustrates how + [subject] + varied / changed + across / over ...
items.example: The bar chart illustrates how the occupational earnings for doctors and other workers varied across seven nations in 2004.
The provided maps illustrate the structural changes and developments that occurred at Queen Mary Hospital across three distinct years: 1960, 1980, and 2000.
items.note: Teacher's map introduction frame.

items.phrase: The diagram illustrates the step-by-step process of ...
items.example: The diagram illustrates the step-by-step process of brick production for the building industry.
items.note: Teacher's process introduction frame.

items.pattern: The [chart 1] shows ..., while the [chart 2] shows ...
items.example: The line graph shows the number of visits to and from the United Kingdom between 1979 and 1999, while the bar chart shows the five most popular holiday countries for UK residents in 1999.

items.pattern: The [chart 1] indicates ..., and the [chart 2] illustrates ...
items.example: The pie chart indicates four primary causes of farmland becoming degraded in the world, and the table illustrates how they affected different regions in the 1990s.

items.phrase: The diagrams illustrate the processes involved in ... and the subsequent ...
items.example: The diagrams illustrate the processes involved in the production of cement and the subsequent use of cement in the creation of concrete for construction purposes.
items.note: Two process diagrams in one sentence.

when: Change the nouns of the question into synonyms in the introduction

items.example: The bar chart illustrates the quantity of books sold in four European countries between 1995 and 2005.
items.note: Teacher's paraphrase table: number of -> quantity of; amount of -> quantity of.

items.example: The line graph shows the quantity of money spent on books in Germany, France, Italy and Austria from 1995 to 2005.
The line graph illustrates the proportion of Australian exports to four distinct countries.
items.note: Teacher: percentage -> rate / proportion.

items.example: The table presents data on literacy rates by region and gender for 2000-2004.
... to four distinct countries, namely Japan, the United States, China, and India, ...
items.note: Name the categories with 'namely' when there are only a few.

items.example: The line graph presents data on the percentage of people residing in Australia who came from different parts of the world.
items.note: Paraphrase verbs too: living -> residing; travelling -> commuting; using -> utilizing.

items.phrase: the main methods of transportation -> different modes of transportation
items.example: The pie charts illustrate the percentage of students and staff utilizing different modes of transportation to travel to a university in 2004 and 2009.

items.phrase: classified by gender / by region / by age group
items.example: The table illustrates the percentages of people in different age groups in a town who rode bicycles in 2011, classified by gender.
items.note: Useful for tables with two variables (rows and columns).

when: Rewrite the dates of the question in the introduction

items.example: The graph shows the number of tourists between 2005 and 2010.
items.note: Teacher's paraphrase table.

items.example: ... over the period from 1990 to 2012.
items.note: Teacher's favourite time paraphrase in the model answers.

items.example: The bar chart illustrates the populations of seals, whales, and dolphins documented in the Strait of Gormez over a twelve-year period from 2006 to 2018.

items.phrase: in 1985 and 1995 -> in the years 1985 and 1995
items.example: The pie charts compare household spending in the years 1985 and 1995.
items.note: Teacher's paraphrase table.

items.example: ... at Queen Mary Hospital across three distinct years: 1960, 1980, and 2000.
The maps illustrate the structural developments that have taken place in the city of Nelson from 2000 to the present day.
items.note: For 'then and now' maps; use the present perfect in this case.

items.example: The bar chart illustrates how the occupational earnings for doctors and other workers varied across seven nations in 2004.
items.note: A single year = static chart: no trend verbs, use comparison language.

when: Paragraph 2 - the most important paragraph for Task Achievement

items.example: Overall, an upward trend was seen in the percentage of Australian goods exported to India and China, while the US and Japan witnessed an opposite trend over the period shown.
items.note: Start the overview with 'Overall,'. 1-2 sentences only.

items.example: Overall, private cars were the most popular means of transport at the beginning of the period, while they were overtaken by buses as the primary choice in the final year.
items.note: Teacher's rule: NO NUMBER/PERCENTAGE/YEAR in the overview. Say 'at the beginning / in the final year' instead of years.

items.example: Overall, while the proportion of immigrants from the UK declined steadily throughout the period, the figures for Asia and other regions generally increased.
items.note: Teacher's rule: mention the general direction of each group.

items.example: Overall, service industries held the largest market share by a wide margin, whereas sports accounted for the smallest percentage of applicants in the same year.
items.note: Teacher's rule: mention the biggest and smallest category or a change of leader.

items.example: Overall, whereas the proportion of citizens from the UK saw a downward trend, that of Asia and other regions experienced substantial upward trends over the mentioned period.
items.note: Teacher's rule: use while / whereas to contrast two groups.

items.example: In addition, at the beginning, Japan was the main importer of Australian goods, whereas in the last year China surpassed it and ranked first.
items.note: Optional second overview sentence about ranking or extremes.

items.phrase: It is clear that ... / It is apparent that ...
items.example: Overall, it is clear that demand for electricity was much higher in winter than in summer throughout the day.
items.note: Common alternative overview opener (standard IELTS).

when: Overview of a chart with years (line graph, bar/pie/table over time); with projected years mention the past trend AND the projection, no numbers

items.phrase: an upward trend was seen in ..., while ... witnessed an opposite trend
items.pattern: Overall, an upward trend was seen in [A], while [B] witnessed an opposite trend over the period shown.
items.example: Overall, an upward trend was seen in the percentage of Australian goods exported to India and China, while the US and Japan witnessed an opposite trend over the period shown.

items.phrase: X increased, whereas the figure for Y decreased
items.example: The percentage of people traveling by bus, train, walking and bicycle increased, whereas the figure for car decreased over the five-year period.

items.phrase: all ... experienced growth, with X witnessing the most dramatic increase
items.pattern: Overall, all [categories] experienced [growth/decline], with [X] witnessing the most dramatic [increase].
items.example: Overall, all three marine species experienced population growth over the period, with dolphins witnessing the most dramatic increase.

items.phrase: X declined steadily throughout the period, while the figures for Y generally increased
items.example: Overall, while the proportion of immigrants from the UK declined steadily throughout the period, the figures for Asia and other regions generally increased.

items.phrase: despite some fluctuations, X ended slightly higher than its initial level
items.example: Despite some fluctuations, the total percentage ended slightly higher than its initial level.

items.phrase: all ... experienced upward trends over the [40]-year timeframe
items.example: Additionally, Eldan Ltd, Bamforth Ltd, and Finsbury Ltd all experienced upward trends over the 40-year timeframe.

items.phrase: X started at the highest point, but ended at the lowest one
items.example: Whilst the UK started at the highest point, it ended at the lowest one.
items.note: Handout overview version 1 for the residents graph.

items.phrase: ... increased and is expected to keep rising until the end of the period
items.example: Overall, the proportion of the population living in cities increased in all four countries and is expected to keep rising until the end of the period.

items.phrase: ... is predicted to overtake ... by the end of the period
items.example: Overall, the urban population of Indonesia is predicted to overtake that of the Philippines by the end of the period.
items.note: Standard example of the same structure.

category: Overview: highest, lowest and change of leader
when: The MAX/MIN part of the overview, a change in ranking, or the main comparison in a static chart (one year)

items.phrase: X was the main ..., whereas in the last year Y surpassed it and ranked first
items.example: At the beginning, Japan was the main importer of Australian goods, whereas in the last year China surpassed it and ranked first.

items.phrase: X was the most popular ... at the beginning, while it was overtaken by Y as the primary choice in the final year
items.example: Overall, private cars were the most popular means of transport at the beginning of the period, while they were overtaken by buses as the primary choice in the final year.

items.phrase: as a result of a sharp rise, X surpassed that of Y to become the highest
items.example: In addition, as a result of a sharp rise, the number of dolphins surpassed that of seals to become the highest one in the final year.

items.phrase: held the largest share by a wide margin
items.example: Overall, service industries held the largest market share by a wide margin, whereas sports accounted for the smallest percentage of applicants.
The United States topped the list for both doctors and other workers in terms of annual income.

items.phrase: X accounted for the largest percentage by the end of the period, whereas Y saw the lowest rate
items.example: Overall, women holding senior management positions in Eldan Ltd accounted for the largest percentage by the end of the period, whereas Finsbury Ltd saw the lowest rate of the three in the final year.
However, UK residents traveling abroad always outnumbered foreign visitors.

items.phrase: ..., with X being the most significant
items.example: Overall, over-grazing, deforestation, and over-cultivation were the three major contributors to land degradation, with over-grazing being the most significant.

items.phrase: X consistently commanded higher ... than Y in all ...
items.example: Overall, physicians consistently commanded higher salaries than other professionals in all countries surveyed.

items.phrase: ..., while ... was relatively similar and low for both categories
items.example: The United States topped the list for both doctors and other workers in terms of annual income, while income in Italy, the Czech Republic, Germany and Finland was relatively similar and low for both categories.

items.phrase: X, regardless of ..., were more likely to ...
items.example: Overall, younger individuals, regardless of gender, were more likely to ride bicycles, with the highest proportions seen in the 0-9 age group.

items.phrase: X generally ... more than Y across all ..., with the most significant gap observed among ...
items.example: Additionally, females generally cycled more than males across all age groups, with the most significant gender gap observed among teenagers.

items.phrase: Among the regions, X experienced the highest ..., whereas Y had the least
items.example: Among the regions, Europe experienced the highest percentage of land degradation, whereas North America had the least.

when: Map overview: the most significant change, no data or years. Say whether the area became more urbanized, commercialized, accessible or industrialized

items.phrase: transformed from a primarily rural settlement into ...
items.example: Overall, the village transformed from a primarily rural settlement into a highly developed, modern residential town.
items.note: Urbanization / residential development.

items.phrase: experienced significant urbanization ... at the expense of agricultural land
items.example: Overall, the area experienced significant urbanization, characterized by a substantial increase in housing infrastructure at the expense of agricultural land.

items.phrase: saw a dramatic shift from ... to ...
items.example: Overall, the landscape saw a dramatic shift from open countryside to an extensive residential estate with modernized amenities.

items.phrase: underwent a major redevelopment, shifting its focus toward ...
items.example: Overall, the resort underwent a major redevelopment, shifting its focus entirely toward tourist accommodations and leisure activities.
items.note: Commercialization / leisure expansion.

items.example: Overall, the town center became heavily commercialized, with a variety of new retail spaces and recreational facilities replacing the older, traditional structures.

items.phrase: was completely transformed from ... into a prominent industrial hub
items.example: Overall, the northern district was completely transformed from a quiet residential zone into a prominent industrial hub.
items.note: Industrialization / change of purpose.

items.phrase: was entirely cleared to make way for ...
items.example: Overall, the town underwent a total transformation as its central industrial sector was entirely cleared to make way for a pedestrianized commercial zone.

items.phrase: transport infrastructure was vastly improved, making ... more accessible
items.example: Overall, the region's transport infrastructure was vastly improved, making the eastern side of the river much more accessible.
items.note: Infrastructure / accessibility.

items.phrase: while the core buildings remained unchanged, the surrounding layout was modernized
items.example: Overall, while the core buildings remained unchanged, the surrounding layout was modernized with a highly interconnected road network.

items.phrase: the interior of the building was restructured to create an open-plan layout
items.example: Overall, the interior of the building was restructured to create an open-plan layout with a stronger focus on technology and public spaces.
items.note: Internal building layout (floor plans).

items.phrase: underwent significant modernization over the [40]-year period
items.example: Overall, the entire area underwent significant modernization over the 40-year period.
items.note: Avoid the number in a real overview: 'over the period shown' is safer.

items.phrase: X is situated in a rural environment ..., whereas Y is centrally located within an urban zone
items.example: Overall, S1 is situated in a rural environment on the outskirts of the city, whereas S2 is centrally located within an urban zone.
items.note: Two possible sites (static map): present simple.

when: Process overview: number of stages + first stage + last stage (+ simple / complex)

items.phrase: Overall, there are (7) stages in the process, beginning with ... and culminating in ...
items.pattern: Overall, there are [N] stages/steps in the process, beginning with ______ and culminating in ______.
items.example: Overall, the production involves nine key stages, beginning with raw material extraction and culminating in delivery.
items.note: Teacher's process overview formula.

items.example: Overall, hydroelectric power is generated using natural water cycles through a multi-stage procedure, beginning with the evaporation of sea water and ending with the final distribution of electricity.

items.phrase: X is more complex than Y, involving ...; conversely, Y is comparatively straightforward
items.example: Overall, the process of cement-making is more complex than concrete production, involving more than six stages and specific equipment. Conversely, the concrete mixing process is comparatively straightforward.
items.note: Two diagrams: compare their complexity in the overview.

items.example: Overall, honey production is a natural process consisting of seven stages, from building the hive to the final product for human consumption.
items.note: Say whether the process is natural (cycle) or man-made (manufacturing).

when: Describing a rise over time (line graph, bar chart, table with years)

items.pattern: X increased from A to B (between YEAR and YEAR)
items.example: The number of visitors increased from 2 million in 2000 to 5 million in 2010.
items.note: Noun: an increase in X / an increase of 20% (size).

items.example: The number of books rose to 90000 in Italy in 2000.
items.note: rise - rose - risen (irregular; never 'rised'). Noun: a rise in X.

items.example: Similarly, exports to India grew steadily from about 2 billion to around 7 billion in 2010.
items.note: Noun 'growth' is uncountable: 'substantial growth' (no 'a').

items.example: However, this figure saw a decline to about 35 in 2014 before climbing again to nearly 50 by 2018.
The percentage of people using their phones to access the Internet jumped to 41% in 2008.
items.note: A sudden, large rise.

items.example: Literacy rates improved considerably in Asia over the period.
items.note: Only for positive things (rates of success, quality).

items.example: The number went up by 600 from 1,200 to 1,800.
By 2012, they had surged to approximately 27 billion, overtaking Japan and the US.
items.note: A sudden, very large rise.

items.example: Cases shot up from 2,400 in 1996 to 4,000 in 2004.
items.note: Very fast rises. Use once per report at most.

items.phrase: an upward trend was observed in
items.example: An increase / an upward trend was observed in the number of books in Germany in 2000, standing at 120000.
items.note: Teacher's noun pattern.

items.phrase: exhibited a steady upward trend, starting at ... and reaching ...
items.example: The whale population exhibited a steady upward trend, starting at 15 in 2006 and reaching 30 by 2018.

when: Describing a fall over time

items.example: However, this figure decreased consistently over the period, reaching around 17 billion in 2012.
In 2009, the rate of unemployment fell by 2% (from 10% to 8%).
items.note: fall - fell - fallen. Do not confuse 'fell' with 'felt'.

items.example: However, this figure saw a decline to about 35 in 2014.
From 1990 to 2000, there was a drop of 15%.
After this peak, it dipped again to 20% in 2000 and rebounded to 26% in 2015.
items.note: A small, short fall followed by recovery.

items.example: The figure went down to 30% in 2015 before rising again.
Coal production plummeted to just 5 million tonnes by 2010.
items.note: A very sharp fall. 'plummet' is in the teacher's verb table; 'plunge' is a standard synonym.

items.example: The statistics show a reduction of 20% in energy costs as a result of the measures.
There have been dramatic cuts in the level of spending on the elderly, reaching a low of 11%.
Overall, whereas the proportion of citizens from the UK saw a downward trend, that of Asia and other regions experienced substantial upward trends.

when: When the figure goes up and down with no clear direction

items.pattern: X fluctuated between A and B (+ time)
items.example: The number of books fluctuated between 70000 and 90000 in Italy in the first two years.
items.note: Teacher's board example.

items.example: Monthly rainfall varied between 20 mm and 150 mm over the year.
The figures for imprisonment fluctuated sharply over the period shown.
There was a slight fluctuation in the number of visitors in the first half of the year.

items.phrase: remained between A and B throughout the period
items.example: Total numbers remained between 19 and 25 million throughout the period with a low point in 1996 and a peak in 2011.

items.phrase: exports fluctuated. They started at ..., fell to ..., then recovered to ...
items.example: Meanwhile, exports to the US fluctuated. They started at about 11 billion, fell to 8 billion in 1995, then recovered to roughly the same level in 2000 before declining slightly again.
items.note: Describe the key points of a fluctuating line in order.

items.phrase: exhibited a wide range, from approximately ... to ...
items.example: Doctors' annual salaries exhibited a wide range across the seven countries, from approximately $50,000 to $120,000.

when: When a figure stays the same

items.pattern: X remained stable at [value] (+ time)
items.example: The number of books remained stable at 90000 in Italy in the first two years.
items.note: Teacher's board example.

items.example: For twenty years, the number of employees remained the same.
The number of cars sold remained unchanged in 1999 at three million.
The price of bread remained static at $2 for five years.
After a sharp fall, the price of oil stabilized at around $70 a barrel.
Oil production rose dramatically at first but then leveled out at $70 a barrel.
A period of stability followed between 2005 and 2008, with the figure staying at roughly 40%.
items.note: Noun form from the teacher's table.

items.example: In the period from 1990 to 1995, the birth rate remained relatively stable at around 12 per thousand.
The car park remained unaltered.
items.note: Useful for maps.

items.example: From 1950 to 1960, there was no change in energy use.

category: Trends: peaks, lowest points and recovery
when: Highest and lowest points on a line and a rise after a fall

items.pattern: X peaked at [value] in [year] / X reached a peak of [value] in [year]
items.example: GM car sales peaked at 2,000 in 1999.
items.note: 'peaked AT' a value, 'a peak OF' a value.

items.phrase: reaching a peak of ... before ending slightly lower at ...
items.example: This trend increased gradually over the following years, reaching a peak of around 14% in 2006 before ending slightly lower at about 13% in 2011.
Unemployment reached its highest level in 2008, at 10%.
The number of students fell to a low of 1,500 in the second half of the year.

items.phrase: the lowest point / a low point
items.example: Total numbers remained between 19 and 25 million throughout the period with a low point in 1996 and a peak in 2011.

items.phrase: from a low of ... to a high of ...
items.example: Profits rose from a low of 4.5 million to a high of 8 million in 2008.
Exports fell to 8 billion in 1995, then recovered to roughly the same level in 2000.
After this peak, it dipped again to 20% in 2000 and rebounded to 26% in 2015.
The unemployment rate bottomed out at 4% in 2007 before rising again.
items.note: Standard phrase: reach the lowest point and then stop falling.

items.example: This growth continued dramatically, culminating in 55 dolphins recorded in 2018.

when: Adjectives (before a noun) and adverbs (after a verb) for big or fast changes

items.example: There was a significant increase in sales, which rose significantly to 40,000.
items.note: adjective + noun: a significant increase; verb + adverb: increased significantly.

items.example: The number of cinema visits dropped dramatically to 2 million in 2015.
items.note: Teacher's example: a dramatic improvement / dropped dramatically.

items.example: However, this figure decreased considerably to 28% in 2009.
Exports to China rose sharply throughout the period.
A rapid decrease / a rapid downward trend was seen in the use of desktop computers.
items.note: Teacher's board example: 'A rapid decrease / a rapid downward trend'.

items.example: Before 1960 the number remained small, but after 1965 there was a sudden increase.
Sales rose steeply in the final year.
The dolphin population experienced substantial growth throughout the period.
There was a marked rise in the number of students studying abroad.
items.note: Standard synonym of 'noticeable'.

items.example: Sales went up noticeably after 2003, reaching approximately 95 million.

category: Size and speed: small or moderate changes
when: Adjectives and adverbs for small, slow or regular changes

items.example: It dropped slightly to 14% in 1980.
items.note: Teacher's example: fluctuated slightly / a slight fluctuation.

items.example: This trend increased gradually over the following years.
Immigration from Asia rose steadily from 6% in 1976 to around 10% in 1996.
items.note: Teacher's example: a steady growth / increased steadily.

items.example: The whale population rose moderately to roughly 20 in 2010.
The number of members rose slowly during the first decade.
Train travel grew marginally to 4% by the end of the period.
The proportion from the UK fell consistently over the following decades.
Exports to India increased steadily before experiencing a minor decline in the final years.
There was a negligible drop in coal use between 2001 and 2002.
items.note: So small it hardly matters.

items.example: It grew continuously in the following years to reach 64% in 2015.

category: Two sentence patterns for every trend
when: Vary your report: use both the verb pattern and the noun pattern (teacher's board notes)

items.pattern: Subject + verb + adverb (+ from A to B / by X + time)
items.example: The number of tourists increased significantly between 2000 and 2010.
items.note: e.g. increased significantly, rose steeply, improved considerably, jumped suddenly, fluctuated slightly, fell rapidly, dropped dramatically, dipped sharply.

items.pattern: There was a/an + adjective + noun + in + subject (+ time)
items.example: There was a significant increase in the number of tourists between 2000 and 2010.
items.note: e.g. a dramatic improvement, a sudden increase, a rapid rise, a steady growth, a slight fluctuation, a gradual decrease, a steep drop, a sharp decline.

items.phrase: An increase / An upward trend was observed in ...
items.pattern: A/An + (adjective) + noun + was observed in + subject, standing at [value]
items.example: An increase was observed in the number of books in Germany in 2000, standing at 120000.

items.phrase: Subject + saw / experienced / witnessed + adjective + noun
items.example: The dolphin population experienced substantial growth throughout the period.
The period between 1997 and 2001 saw a steady rise in the figure.
items.note: Standard variation: the time phrase becomes the subject.

items.pattern: Subject + saw + (adjective) + noun + to/of + value
items.example: However, this figure saw a decline to about 35 in 2014 before climbing again to nearly 50 by 2018.
In contrast to seals and whales, the dolphin population experienced substantial growth throughout the period.
Japan witnessed an opposite trend over the period shown.

items.phrase: there was / there has been + adj + noun + in
items.pattern: There was a [sudden/sharp/steady] [increase/decline] in + subject
items.example: There was a sudden increase in the number of applications after 1965.

items.phrase: ... made up an increase / made up a significant rise
items.example: The figure for Germany made up a significant rise in 2005.
items.note: Teacher's board notes: 'Verbs + noun / adj + noun (experience)'.

items.example: Walking to the campus accounted for just 4% of journeys in 2004 before experiencing a slight rise to 6% in 2009.

items.phrase: it experienced a sharp increase to reach
items.example: It experienced a sharp increase to reach 46% by 2009, making it the top transit method.

when: Choosing to / by / at / of / with / from...to / between...and correctly (teacher's photographed sheet)

items.example: In 2008, the rate of unemployment rose to 10%.
items.note: Use TO for what happened to the number (the new level).

items.phrase: fell by (the size of the change)
items.example: In 2009, the rate of unemployment fell by 2% (from 10% to 8%).
items.note: Use BY for the amount of change between two numbers.

items.phrase: at (the number at the end of a sentence)
items.example: Unemployment reached its highest level in 2008, at 10%.
He won the election with 52% of the vote.
From 1990 to 2000, there was a drop of 15%.
items.note: Noun + OF + amount: a decline of 35%, an increase of 50,000.

items.phrase: a rise / fall in (the thing that changes)
items.example: There has been a significant increase in the number of people aged over eighty.
items.note: Noun + IN + subject: a decline of 35% in the bird population.

items.example: Cases of AIDS shot up from 2,400 in 1996 to 4,000 in 2004.
Canada and Australia's wheat exports fluctuated between 5 million and 6 million respectively.
In 2006, the seal population stood at approximately 27.
Demand reached a peak of 45,000 in early March.
Profits fell by 10%, from 2,000 to 1,800 in the 1970s.

items.phrase: a fall of ... to a total of ...
items.example: The radio station experienced a fall of 36,000 listeners to a total audience of 2.1 million.

when: Choosing the right subject word (teacher's board notes: (c) = countable, (uc) = uncountable)

items.pattern: The number of + plural countable noun + SINGULAR verb
items.example: The number of people out of work fell by 99,000 to 2.39 million in the three months to October.
items.note: the number of tourists / cars / students. NEVER 'the number of money'.

items.pattern: The amount of + uncountable noun + singular verb
items.example: The amount of rainfall doubles between May and June.
items.note: the amount of money / water / electricity.

items.example: The quantity of money spent on books rose steadily.
items.note: Works with both countable and uncountable nouns: the quantity of money is correct.

items.pattern: The percentage of + noun + singular verb
items.example: The percentage of people using their phones to access the Internet jumped to 41% in 2008.
The proportion of spending on furniture and equipment reached its peak in 2001, at 23%.
The rate of unemployment rose to 10% in 2008.
items.note: Also: literacy rate, crime rate, birth rate.

items.pattern: The figures for + noun + PLURAL verb
items.example: The figures for imprisonment fluctuated sharply over the period shown.
The share of people traveling by bicycle saw a significant climb, rising from 9% to 16%.

items.phrase: Number / Quantity / Amount; Percentage / Proportion / Rate; Figure / Indicator
items.example: The indicator for Italy varied from approximately 50 in 1995 to just over 60 in 2005.
items.note: Teacher's list of 'quantities' - synonyms to rotate for the subject.

category: Avoiding repetition: the figure for, that of
when: Refer back to a subject without repeating it

items.example: The amount of money spent on books was 90 in Germany in 2000, while the figure for Austria was twice less than that of Germany, standing at 45 in the same year.
items.note: Teacher: 'The figure/indicator + for = paraphrase the subject'.

items.example: The indicator for Brazil rose to a peak of 20% in 2010.

items.phrase: that of + X (singular) / those of + X (plural)
items.example: The number of dolphins surpassed that of seals to become the highest one in the final year.
items.note: 'that of' replaces 'the number of'; use 'those of' for a plural noun.

items.example: Among those aged 10-17, the proportion of female cyclists remained relatively high at 42.2%, whereas the corresponding figure for males was considerably lower, at 24.6%.
However, this figure decreased considerably to 28% in 2009.
Cars and buses were the main modes of transport; the former declined, while the latter grew.
items.note: Standard: 'the former' = the first of two, 'the latter' = the second.

items.example: The figures for transportation & warehousing and science & technology comprised 7.8% and 7.3% respectively.
items.note: Gives the numbers in the same order as the categories.

category: Verbs for giving a value or a share
when: Saying how big a figure or part of a whole is (pie charts, tables, static bar charts)

items.example: The amount of money spent on books was 90 in Germany in 2000.
items.note: Teacher's list: was / made up / constituted / consisted of.

items.example: The figure for Germany makes up 40%.
The proportion of graduates who opted for service industries constituted exactly one-third of the total (33%).
Cars accounted for over half of all university commutes in 2004, at 51%.
items.note: The most useful verb for pie charts. Also: accounted for the majority.

items.example: The figures for transportation & warehousing and science & technology comprised 7.8% and 7.3% respectively.
items.note: No 'of' after comprise (comprise 7.8%, not 'comprised of').

items.example: The concrete mixture consists of 50% gravel, 25% sand, 15% cement and 10% water.

items.phrase: amount to / equal / be equal to
items.example: Spending on health care was equal to 3% in both countries.
Deforestation followed closely at 30%, while over-cultivation represented 28%.
The percentage of female senior managers in Finsbury Ltd stood at 16% in 1975.
A smaller proportion, 7%, was attributed to other causes.
Train travel was the least popular option, utilized by a mere 3% of travelers.
Service industries held the largest market share by a wide margin.

when: When the value falls between gridlines - do not invent exact numbers

category: Multiples, fractions of change and percentage points

when: First words of body paragraphs 1 and 2 - show which group, area, period or chart you describe (mixed charts: one paragraph per chart)

when: Which preposition goes with which time expression (teacher's time-expressions sheet)

when: Tense depends on the time of the data and on the preposition (teacher's board notes)

items.phrase: Past data + in / from...to / between...and / during / throughout / over / at / around -> past simple

items.phrase: Future data + the same prepositions -> will + verb

items.phrase: by / until + past year -> past perfect (had + V3)
items.example: The amount of money spent on books had risen to 90 in Germany by 2000.

items.phrase: by + future year -> future perfect (will have + V3)
items.example: The amount of money spent on books will have risen to 90 in Germany by 2030.

items.example: Since 2000, the number of cyclists has risen steadily.
The adjacent eastern woodland has been cleared to make way for a new shopping center.

items.phrase: Subject + will + verb + object + preposition + time
